course.title: Speed, Agility & Change of Direction
course.owner: JR Romero, CSCS - Director of Training
course.evidence_pack: G3-103 Speed, Agility and Change of Direction Evidence Pack FINAL
course.purpose: Teach coaches to understand, distinguish, develop, assess, and coach the speed and multidirectional movement qualities that appear in athletic performance - without collapsing them into 'speed and agility'.
course.sequence_note: Conceptual organizer for classification. NOT a mandatory training progression.
course.prerequisite: G3 102 complete including T-01; active G3 Performance coaching status
course.delivery: NovaKore self-paced modules with four observed practical sign-offs (PS-1 to PS-4) plus the final oral defense (T-01).
five_task_identification_questions: What velocity is involved, and where does it come from?
Is velocity being built, held, or reduced?
Is direction changing, and is the change known in advance?
What information must the athlete perceive to solve the task?
What is the intended adaptation, and does the task's demand match it?
outcomes: CO-1 Define and distinguish acceleration, maximal velocity, deceleration, COD, and agility
CO-2 Identify the primary performance demand of a drill, test, or training task
CO-3 Explain acceleration and maximal-velocity mechanics without converting correlations into universal prescriptions
CO-4 Design basic acceleration and maximal-velocity exposures
CO-5 Select resisted sprint methods by intended adaptation without a universal load rule
CO-6 Integrate strength and plyometric methods as supporting contributors
CO-7 Coach and progress deceleration demands
CO-8 Distinguish COD training from agility training
CO-9 Manipulate approach velocity, cut angle, braking, reacceleration, and information demand
CO-10 Design reactive agility tasks with meaningful perception-action requirements
CO-11 Select tests matching the construct evaluated
CO-12 Interpret results within reliability and measurement limits
CO-13 Design developmentally appropriate youth speed and multidirectional work
CO-14 Organize work to protect intended output quality
CO-16 Defend a speed-development prescription using evidence, G3 standards, and athlete context

inherited_rules: training exists to create relevant adaptation, not merely fatigue
specificity is based on correspondence to target demands, not visual resemblance
progression is purposeful manipulation of demand relative to capacity
multiple qualities may be trained concurrently
evidence, G3 Applied Standard, and Coach Judgment must remain distinguishable
testing should inform decisions without pretending to reveal more than the measurement supports
foundations_continuity.decision_model_source: G3 102 - inherited unchanged; G3 103 supplies domain content per stage
foundations_continuity.conflict_rule: Where G3 103 and G3 102 appear to disagree, G3 102 is authoritative.

evidence_classes.name: Established Evidence
evidence_classes.teaching_rule: May be taught as established, bounded by population and task.

evidence_classes.name: Supported Practice
evidence_classes.teaching_rule: Taught as well-supported practice with the moderator stated.

evidence_classes.name: Emerging / Conditional Evidence
evidence_classes.teaching_rule: Taught as conditional; never the sole basis for a required behavior.

evidence_classes.name: Applied Coaching Inference
evidence_classes.teaching_rule: Taught explicitly as inference, labeled aloud.

evidence_classes.name: Historical / Practitioner Framework
evidence_classes.teaching_rule: Taught as framework and history; never as proof.

evidence_classes.name: Unsupported / Overstated Claim
evidence_classes.teaching_rule: NEVER taught as true. Used only to name and correct the error.

description_to_prescription_rule: A statement of the form 'faster athletes display X' may never be rendered as 'coach X' without intervention evidence in a comparable population. Where G3 coaches X anyway, it is a labeled Applied Standard or Coach Judgment with the descriptive basis stated.

doctrine.title: Speed Is Phase-Specific
doctrine.statement: Acceleration and maximal velocity are related but distinct sprint qualities. Coaches identify which speed demand is being trained or assessed rather than treating sprint performance as one undifferentiated quality.
doctrine.teaching_boundary: The distinction is established; exact phase boundaries are not. G3 publishes no universal distance cut-point.

doctrine.title: Exposure Is Irreplaceable
doctrine.statement: General strength, power, and plyometric training can support sprint development, but they do not fully replace sprint-specific exposure when the desired adaptation is sprint performance.
doctrine.teaching_boundary: Not a claim that the weight room is unimportant, and not a dose statement. Sets no minimum sprint volume (CJ-01).

doctrine.title: Mechanics Inform; They Do Not Dictate
doctrine.statement: Biomechanics can describe characteristics associated with better sprint performance. A descriptive characteristic does not automatically become a causal coaching target. G3 does not impose one universal sprint-mechanics model on every athlete.
doctrine.teaching_boundary: Descriptive support is A-class; technique-intervention evidence is limited by comparison; universalizing an elite track model is F. Technique coaching is not forbidden - gating exposure on it is.

doctrine.title: Deceleration Is a Performance Quality
doctrine.statement: Deceleration is not merely the first half of a COD drill. Braking capacity, momentum control, approach velocity, posture, and eccentric demands justify treating deceleration as a distinct training and assessment consideration.
doctrine.teaching_boundary: Distinctness is A; diagnostics and the qualities that best develop it are C. No progression ladder is evidence-derived; AS-103-05 is an applied standard.

doctrine.title: COD Is Not Agility
doctrine.statement: Pre-planned COD and agility are different constructs. COD involves a known movement solution. Agility requires perception, decision, and response to external information.
doctrine.teaching_boundary: Distinct does not mean unrelated. The doctrine forbids treating them as the same, not as connected.

doctrine.title: Closed Drills Do Not Automatically Train Agility
doctrine.statement: Cone patterns, ladders, and pre-planned movement drills may train coordination, rhythm, movement skill, or COD. They are not labeled true agility development unless meaningful external information and response demands are present.
doctrine.teaching_boundary: Closed drills are not condemned. The error is the label, not the drill.

doctrine.title: Transfer Is Demand-Based, Not Appearance-Based
doctrine.statement: A drill does not transfer because it looks athletic or resembles sport. Transfer claims are tied to relevant force-time, velocity, coordination, braking, movement, or perception-action demands.
doctrine.teaching_boundary: Not a rejection of specificity - a rejection of resemblance as evidence of it. Inherited from G3 102 Doctrine 5.

doctrine.title: Speed Quality Requires Quality Exposure
doctrine.statement: High-speed and high-intensity multidirectional work is generally organized to preserve meaningful output and technical quality. Fatigue is not evidence that speed training became more sport-specific.
doctrine.teaching_boundary: No rest ratio, repetition count, or velocity-decrement threshold is established (CJ-03, CJ-07). Training under fatigue is not forbidden; claiming the fatigue made it specific is.

doctrine.title: Load Serves the Intended Sprint Adaptation
doctrine.statement: Resisted sprinting is a supported training tool, especially for acceleration, but G3 does not adopt one universal sled load or percentage for every athlete and outcome.
doctrine.teaching_boundary: A that RST improves sprint performance; C for loading strategy. No percentage, decrement number, or load table appears anywhere in G3 103. Both absolutist claims rejected (CA-06, CA-07).

doctrine.title: Testing Measures Tasks, Not Labels
doctrine.statement: A sprint split, COD test, or reactive test measures performance under its specific constraints. Coaches do not infer maximal velocity, agility, or isolated physical qualities from a test that does not directly establish them.
doctrine.teaching_boundary: A labeling and inference rule, not a rejection of field testing. No universal smallest-worthwhile-change threshold is created.

doctrine.title: Youth Speed Development Is Readiness- and Development-Aware
doctrine.statement: Youth athletes can improve sprint, COD, and agility-related qualities. Programming considers maturation, coordination, training age, readiness, and exposure history rather than relying on rigid chronological-age windows.
doctrine.teaching_boundary: Rejecting age-window mythology is not a claim that maturation is irrelevant. Youth sprint-mechanics prescriptions remain extrapolated and are labeled (AS-103-12).

doctrine.title: Injury Claims Require Causal Restraint
doctrine.statement: G3 distinguishes tissue demand, association, mechanistic plausibility, risk-factor evidence, and intervention evidence. Sprinting, deceleration, or COD training is not marketed as inherently dangerous or inherently injury-preventive without appropriate evidence.
doctrine.teaching_boundary: Restraint runs both directions: no protection promises, and no withholding exposure on an unsupported danger claim. Binds marketing, parent, and athlete communication.

applied_standards.title: Name the Quality
applied_standards.text: Every speed/COD/agility prescription identifies the primary quality being targeted: acceleration, maximal velocity, deceleration, planned COD, or reactive agility.

applied_standards.title: Preserve Sprint Exposure
applied_standards.text: When sprint performance is a priority, the program includes actual sprint exposure appropriate to the targeted phase rather than relying solely on weight-room or plyometric proxies.
applied_standards.boundary_or_enforcement: sets no volume, distance, or frequency (CJ-01, CJ-02)

applied_standards.title: Technique With Restraint
applied_standards.text: Technique coaching is used to improve task execution. Athletes are not required to conform to a single visual model before meaningful sprint exposure is allowed.
applied_standards.boundary_or_enforcement: restrains the gate, not the coaching

applied_standards.title: Resisted Sprint Intent
applied_standards.text: Resisted sprint load and method are selected according to intended adaptation, athlete capacity, equipment, and output quality. No universal loading percentage is G3 law.
applied_standards.boundary_or_enforcement: CJ-06 owns the number; any percentage stated as a rule fails production review

applied_standards.title: Deceleration Before Directional Complexity
applied_standards.text: Where appropriate, athletes are taught and exposed to braking and momentum-control demands before approach velocity, cut severity, reactive complexity, or total multidirectional density are escalated.
applied_standards.boundary_or_enforcement: explicitly an Applied Standard, NOT a universal research-derived progression ladder (CJ-10)

applied_standards.title: COD Task Specificity
applied_standards.text: COD is programmed and evaluated with awareness of approach velocity, cut angle, braking demand, reacceleration demand, and test/task structure.

applied_standards.title: Agility Requires Information
applied_standards.text: At least part of an agility-development progression requires athletes to perceive relevant information and select and execute a movement response.
applied_standards.boundary_or_enforcement: 'at least part' is deliberate; no proven dose of reactive work is claimed

applied_standards.title: Quality Preservation
applied_standards.text: Rest and repetition structure are sufficient to preserve the intended performance quality. Exact rest ratios are not universal G3 doctrine.
applied_standards.boundary_or_enforcement: criterion is output, not the clock (CJ-03)

applied_standards.title: Testing Standardization
applied_standards.text: G3 testing uses objective timing where practical, standardized setups, familiarization, consistent surfaces and conditions, and known measurement error before small changes are interpreted.
applied_standards.boundary_or_enforcement: no universal smallest-worthwhile-change threshold is created

applied_standards.title: Construct-Appropriate Testing
applied_standards.text: A pre-planned COD test is not called an agility test. A short acceleration split is not called a maximal-velocity test. G3 labels what was actually measured.
applied_standards.boundary_or_enforcement: test_record requires construct_measured; mislabeling is a scored error

applied_standards.title: Multi-Measure Interpretation
applied_standards.text: When profiling multidirectional performance, relevant measures are combined rather than using one test to diagnose all speed, COD, braking, and agility qualities.
applied_standards.boundary_or_enforcement: no battery, weighting, or composite score prescribed

applied_standards.title: Population Transfer Disclosure
applied_standards.text: When a prescription is substantially extrapolated from elite track, adult, soccer-heavy, or male-dominant evidence, the educational content says so.
applied_standards.boundary_or_enforcement: every module evidence block carries a population-transfer line where extrapolation occurs

claim_audit.taught_instead: Sprint and sprint-related qualities are trainable; adaptations vary by quality and population.

claim_audit.claim: Athletes either have speed or they do not
claim_audit.taught_instead: Athlete qualities differ, and sprint performance responds to multiple training methods.
Strength transfers partially and outcome-specifically; it does not replace sprint exposure.

claim_audit.claim: Horizontal force is all that matters in acceleration
claim_audit.taught_instead: Horizontal impulse and force orientation matter within a whole-system task.

claim_audit.claim: Vertical force is all that matters at maximal velocity
claim_audit.taught_instead: Vertical force is important; top speed is not reducible to one variable.

claim_audit.claim: Heavier resisted sprint loads are always better
claim_audit.taught_instead: Load magnitude matters; no universal monotonic rule is established.
RST can improve acceleration; the blanket negative claim is unsupported.

claim_audit.claim: Overspeed is necessary for top-speed development
claim_audit.taught_instead: Evidence is limited and does not establish superiority over normal sprinting.
Ladders may train footwork rhythm and coordination - useful, and not agility.

claim_audit.claim: Cone drills are automatically agility training
claim_audit.taught_instead: Pre-planned cone work trains COD unless reactive information is added.

claim_audit.claim: COD and agility are the same
claim_audit.taught_instead: Distinct constructs; agility requires perception and decision.

claim_audit.claim: The fastest linear sprinter should automatically have the best COD
claim_audit.taught_instead: COD is influenced by braking, angle, technique, orientation, and reacceleration beyond linear speed.

claim_audit.claim: Every athlete needs the same sprint mechanics
claim_audit.taught_instead: Descriptive elite mechanics do not become one universal model.

claim_audit.claim: Perfect technique must precede meaningful speed exposure
claim_audit.taught_instead: Exposure is not gated on a universal technique threshold; coaching happens alongside it.

claim_audit.claim: Fatigued sprint work is automatically more sport-specific
claim_audit.taught_instead: Fatigue changes mechanics; the specificity claim is unsupported. Quality preservation is better supported.
Risk exists and is managed through exposure and preparation; blanket danger claims exceed the evidence.
Exposure and eccentric capacity are relevant; prevention guarantees exceed intervention evidence.
Variation may aid engagement and adaptability; a universal need for novelty is unsupported.
Transfer depends on relevant demands, not appearance.

claim_audit_symmetry_rule: Every correction is a correction, not an inversion. Correcting a Class F claim by asserting its opposite reproduces the error.

competencies.title: Terminology discrimination
competencies.observable_standard: Classifies any drill or test by primary quality using the G3 definitions; never labels a pre-planned task agility.

competencies.title: Sprint-phase analysis
competencies.observable_standard: Identifies whether a task or test targets acceleration or maximal velocity and states why, without asserting a universal phase boundary.

competencies.title: Mechanics interpretation
competencies.observable_standard: Distinguishes a descriptive mechanical finding from an intervention-supported coaching target, and discloses population transfer.

competencies.title: Acceleration prescription
competencies.observable_standard: Designs and delivers an acceleration exposure with named phase, entry condition, intent, and quality criterion.

competencies.title: Max-velocity prescription
competencies.observable_standard: Designs a genuine maximal-velocity exposure or states defensibly why it is not a priority.

competencies.title: Resisted sprint decision-making
competencies.observable_standard: Selects RST method and load by intent, capacity, equipment, and output quality, asserting no universal percentage.

competencies.title: Supporting strength/plyometric integration
competencies.observable_standard: Positions supporting modalities as contributors with stated intended adaptations, never as sprint substitutes.

competencies.title: Deceleration coaching
competencies.observable_standard: Coaches a braking task, manipulates approach velocity, and progresses or regresses with an observable criterion.

competencies.title: COD task design
competencies.observable_standard: Designs COD tasks manipulating entry velocity, angle, braking, and reacceleration, justified by sport demand.

competencies.title: Reactive agility design
competencies.observable_standard: Designs a task in which perceiving relevant information is required to solve it, and says how it differs from the COD version.

competencies.title: Testing selection
competencies.observable_standard: Selects tests matching the construct evaluated and labels outputs accurately.

competencies.title: Measurement interpretation
competencies.observable_standard: Interprets results within reliability and typical error; declines to act inside the noise band; asserts no universal threshold.

competencies.title: Youth/developmental modification
competencies.observable_standard: Applies readiness-based reasoning, rejects age-window claims, and discloses extrapolation.

competencies.title: Session/week integration
competencies.observable_standard: Places speed, braking, and reactive work to protect output quality within a real schedule; asserts no validated microcycle model.

competencies.title: Evidence-boundary recognition
competencies.observable_standard: Identifies unsupported coaching claims and states, for any G3 practice, whether it is evidence, applied standard, or judgment.

competencies.title: Programming defense
competencies.observable_standard: Defends a full speed-development prescription under questioning across the seven obligations.

modules.title: Language Before Programming
modules.framing_statement: Every bad speed program starts with a word.
modules.purpose: To install the controlled vocabulary the rest of the course depends on, and to make the learner capable of naming the quality a task actually trains before any programming decision is made.
objectives: M1.1 Define speed, acceleration, maximal velocity, deceleration, COD, agility, reactive agility using G3 definitions
M1.2 Explain why acceleration and maximal velocity are distinct qualities
M1.3 Explain why COD and agility are distinct constructs
M1.4 Apply the five task-identification questions
M1.5 Describe COD deficit as a task-dependent lens
M1.6 State why G3 does not use SAQ as a precise category
M1.7 Identify where terminology remains unsettled
common_errors: Using 'speed' as the label for every fast activity
Calling a pre-planned cone pattern an agility drill
Treating a 10 m time as top speed
Absorbing deceleration into 'the cut'
Publishing a fixed acceleration/max-velocity boundary
Using COD deficit as an isolate
Using SAQ as a technical taxonomy

gating.prerequisite: G3 102 complete including T-01; active G3 coaching status

modules.title: Understanding Acceleration
modules.framing_statement: Acceleration is the phase most G3 athletes actually live in - and where a real mechanical finding gets flattened into a slogan.
modules.purpose: To give coaches a working understanding of acceleration demands and mechanics accurate enough to inform observation and method selection, without converting descriptive findings into universal cueing prescriptions.
objectives: M2.1 Describe primary acceleration demands
M2.2 Explain horizontal impulse and force orientation without overclaiming
M2.3 Distinguish associational findings from intervention-supported targets
M2.4 Identify physical qualities associated with acceleration
M2.5 Recognize population limits of the acceleration-mechanics literature
M2.6 Identify acceleration demands within a sport or position
common_errors: Coaching 'horizontal force' as a cue
Importing a track sprint-start model wholesale
Treating a correlate as a cause
Assuming every acceleration starts static
Failing to disclose adult track provenance

modules.title: Understanding Maximal Velocity
modules.framing_statement: The quality most often claimed and least often trained.
modules.purpose: To establish maximal velocity as a distinct quality with its own demands and exposure requirement, and to make clear how rarely typical team-sport training or testing actually addresses it.
objectives: M3.1 Describe maximal-velocity demands
M3.2 Explain why maximal velocity is not reducible to one variable
M3.3 Explain why short distances rarely develop or measure maximal velocity
M3.4 State population limits of elite-sprinter evidence
M3.5 Identify what a meaningful maximal-velocity exposure requires
M3.6 Determine whether a sport and athlete need maximal-velocity development

common_errors: Labeling short sprint work as maximal-velocity training

modules.title: Coaching Sprint Mechanics
modules.framing_statement: You are allowed to coach sprinting. You are not allowed to hold an athlete's sprint exposure hostage to a picture in your head.
modules.purpose: To build observation and coaching capability for sprinting that improves task execution while respecting the gap between descriptive biomechanics and intervention evidence, and while preserving meaningful sprint exposure.

common_errors: Running the model without naming the primary quality
A prescription contradicting its own priority in session order
Testing one construct and claiming another
Injury-prevention language in parent or marketing communication
Presenting judgment as evidence under questioning
Unable to name anything that would change the plan

gating.prerequisite: M11 at standard; four-week delivery window complete
gating.gate: T-01 required for course competency completion

cases.title: Middle-School Field/Court Athlete
cases.situation_summary: 12-year-old, two seasonal sports, no training history, high instructional responsiveness, poor braking organization at speed. Group of 16, one coach, two 50-minute sessions. Parent asks about 'proper sprint mechanics work' and sled sprints.
cases.decision_prompt: What does the speed and multidirectional work consist of, what is deliberately excluded, and what do you tell the parent?
failure_modes: Adult track model applied without disclosure
A sled percentage quoted as a rule

cases.title: High-School Athlete With Strong 10 m but Poorer High-Speed Capacity
cases.situation_summary: 16-year-old wide midfielder. 10 m among the best on the team; flying 10 m velocity in the bottom third; consistent across two occasions on the same surface with electronic gates. Program has run 6 x 20 m standing starts labeled 'speed'.
cases.decision_prompt: What quality is actually deficient, what has the program been training, and what changes?
failure_modes: Treating the 10 m result as top-speed evidence
Adding volume rather than changing entry conditions and distance
Attributing the difference to noise when data rules it out
Prescribing max-velocity work with no demand justification

cases.title: Fast Linear Speed, Weak Planned COD
cases.situation_summary: 17-year-old outside back. Among the fastest at 10 m and flying 10 m; among the poorest 505-style results with a large left/right difference and a correspondingly large COD deficit. No pain. Video shows high entry velocity, four short braking steps, upright plant, slow exit.
cases.decision_prompt: What is the probable limiting factor, what would distinguish the candidates, and what is the first block?
failure_modes: Assuming linear speed means no COD work needed
Adding pattern volume without changing the constraint

cases.title: Excellent on Cone Drills, Poor in Live Play
cases.situation_summary: 16-year-old in a reactive defensive role. Best times in the program on every pre-planned drill; consistently a step late in live play, commits early to the wrong side. Physical testing strong. Program has responded by adding faster cone work.
cases.decision_prompt: What is the actual gap, and what does the next block look like?
failure_modes: Adding complexity and calling it information demand
Cues arriving too late to be read
Concluding a physical deficit when testing says otherwise

cases.title: Team With Limited Weekly Training Time
cases.situation_summary: Scholastic squad of 30, in-season. Five practices, one match, two 40-minute G3 slots with one lost roughly every other week. Practice already contains substantial sprinting, braking, and directional change, uncounted. Sport coach wants speed, agility, and conditioning every session.
cases.decision_prompt: What goes in the two slots, what is protected, what is compromised, and what do you tell the sport coach cannot be achieved?

cases.title: Youth Athlete and the Heavy Sled Question
cases.situation_summary: Parent asks what percentage of body weight a 15-year-old with one year of structured training should pull, citing conflicting figures and an article claiming heavy sleds are fastest for acceleration. One sled, 30 m indoor lane.
cases.decision_prompt: What do you say, what do you program, and how do you decide the load?
failure_modes: Treating one pending-verification meta-analysis as settling loading
Dropping sprint exposure for the tool

cases.title: Hamstring / Maximal-Velocity Claim Audit
cases.situation_summary: Draft program copy claims maximal-velocity sprinting prevents hamstring injuries. A second coach argues maximal-velocity sprinting is dangerous for high-school athletes and should be removed. A parent asks whether sprinting is safe after her son's hamstring strain.
cases.decision_prompt: Audit both claims, write the replacement copy, and script the parent conversation.
failure_modes: Softening a prevention claim rather than removing it
Removing max-velocity sprinting to satisfy the danger claim
Treating mechanistic rationale as intervention evidence
Reassurance instead of accuracy with the parent
Publishing external copy without Director of Training approval

sign_offs.title: Sprint Observation & Coaching
observed_behaviors: Distinguishes acceleration from higher-speed sprinting in setup and language
Observes without forcing a universal visual model
Selects a limited number of relevant interventions and holds them long enough to evaluate
Preserves meaningful sprint exposure - athletes actually sprint at intensity
Explains the evidence boundary of any technical intervention
Names the quality being trained without prompting
assessor_questions: Which phase is this exposure targeting, and how do you know?
Why that cue for that athlete?
What would tell you the cue isn't helping?
Where did that model come from, and does it apply to this athlete?

sign_offs.title: Deceleration Coaching
observed_behaviors: Identifies braking demand in momentum and entry-velocity terms
Manipulates approach velocity and complexity deliberately
Selects an appropriate regression or progression and states the criterion
Coaches control and organization rather than 'stop faster'
Avoids injury-prevention overclaims in everything said to athletes
Names AS-103-05 as an applied standard when asked
assessor_questions: What makes this task hard for this athlete?
What are you changing to progress it, and why that variable?
What would you say to a parent who asks whether this prevents knee injuries?
Is the order you're using evidence or G3 standard?

sign_offs.title: COD vs Agility Design
observed_behaviors: Designs and delivers a pre-planned COD task with deliberate entry velocity, angle, and exit demand
Designs and delivers a reactive task where perceiving the information is required to solve it
Identifies the informational difference out loud in perception-action terms
Manipulates movement and decision constraints separately
Labels each construct correctly to athletes and in the session document
Coaches both appropriately
assessor_questions: Which of these is agility, and what makes it so?
What information is the athlete actually reading?
What happens to this task if I remove the cue?
Is this drill complex or is it open - and what is the difference?

sign_offs.title: Integrated Speed Session / Microcycle
sign_offs.function: completion requirement; requires four-week delivery window
observed_behaviors: Identifies primary and secondary qualities unprompted
Organizes exposures to protect output quality and adjusts when quality degrades
Integrates supporting strength and plyometric work with stated intended adaptations
Justifies weekly placement in terms of where high outputs can be expressed
Identifies what remains Coach Judgment
Delivers the session as planned or can say what was traded
assessor_questions: What is the primary quality this week, and what is it costing?
What told you the quality had degraded?
Which placement decisions are evidence and which are your call?
What did practice already give these athletes this week?

terminal_defense.title: Speed, COD & Agility Programming Defense
terminal_defense.format: 20-30 minutes with an approved assessor using the coach's own athlete and artifacts; assessor works the seven obligations in order and probes at least four
mandatory_probes: Name the primary quality in this plan, and show me where it appears in the session order.
This test - what does it actually measure, and what did you claim from it?
Why this method rather than the alternative, and what adaptation are you buying?
Which part of what you just told me is evidence, which is G3 standard, and which is your judgment?
What would make you change this plan? Be specific.
Say what you would tell this athlete's parent about injury risk.
non_compensable_failures: makes an injury-prevention claim on probe 6

assessment_system.design_rule: Applied coaching competencies are never certified by multiple-choice questions alone. No learner passes with a failing score in Application, Coaching, or Defense.

pass_standards.applied: at standard or better, one revision permitted

item_writing_rules: No item answerable from a single memorized sentence outside the knowledge band.
Every scenario item commits the learner before feedback.
Distractors are real coaching errors drawn from the claim audit and module error lists.
No key may depend on a claim classified C, D, or E.
No key may depend on a verification-pending or unmapped source as sole support.
No key may require a Class F claim to be treated as true.
No key may require a number G3 has not established (load, rest, decrement, phase boundary, angle progression, change threshold).
Where multiple answers are defensible, the item is a decision item scored on reasoning.
Every item carries module, competency, doctrine, applied standard, evidence class, level, and key source metadata.

automatic_zero_conditions: a Class F claim presented as true
a universal load, rest ratio, velocity-decrement threshold, phase-boundary distance, angle progression, or change threshold asserted as established
a pre-planned task labeled agility, or an acceleration measure labeled maximal velocity
any injury-prevention guarantee or inherent-danger claim
a descriptive mechanical finding presented as a proven causal coaching target
a composite athlete score or automated training recommendation

coaching_rubric.pass: 11/15, no dimension below 2, never 0 on evidence honesty

defense_rubric.pass: 11/15, no dimension below 2, never 0 on evidence honesty

evidence_integrity.verification_pending_criterion: Dated 2025-2026 (the Evidence Pack's stated sweep of newer reviews not yet deeply indexed), or a repository-hosted record whose DOI/final journal details the pack says should be confirmed.
evidence_integrity.unmapped_handling: Carried at reduced confidence, never used alone. Dependent claims in M6 and M7 rest on EP103-14 and EP103-16, both verified. No assessment key depends on it. Resolve or rewrite before external publication.
evidence_integrity.anchor_rule: Every doctrine, applied standard, and assessment key has at least one verified anchor. No content object rests on verification-pending sources alone.

external_use_gate.gate_requirement: all verification-pending sources confirmed and cite:103 resolved or dependent language rewritten

population_transfer_limitations: adult and elite track sprint-mechanics evidence
research_gaps_taught: direct comparisons among RST loading models

testing_governance.rule: WHAT THE TEST MEASURES != WHAT THE COACH WANTS TO CALL IT

test_constructs.measures: acceleration plus later-phase capability by distance
higher-speed / maximal-velocity performance when appropriately set up
mixture of linear speed, braking, technique, orientation, reacceleration
test_constructs.does_not_establish: agility or any single isolated quality

test_constructs.measures: context for COD relative to linear speed

standardization: recorded conditions at time of testing
known measurement error before interpreting small changes
testing_governance.threshold_prohibition: G3 103 creates no universal smallest-worthwhile-change threshold for any test. Local working figures are environment-scoped Applied Standards with a review date, never evidence-derived.
testing_governance.reporting: Every output carries test, construct measured, conditions, and interpretation limits. No composite score. No automated recommendation.

binding_rules: sprinting is not delayed pending perfect technique
adult elite track mechanics are not assumed to transfer and are disclosed when borrowed
entry to loaded or high-intensity progressions is governed by readiness, not chronological age
well-designed youth speed development is not treated as inherently unsafe, and no protective guarantee is offered

female_athletes.position: G3 applies foundational speed, COD, and agility principles across sexes and does not publish sex-specific programming rules where direct intervention evidence is insufficient. Individual modification proceeds on individual grounds. Deliberate restraint; under review.

population_governance.population_transfer_disclosure: Required at the point of the claim, not as an end-of-module disclaimer (AS-103-12).

progression_governance.no_universal_ladder: G3 supplies variables and worked examples, not a sequence (CJ-09 to CJ-11).
progression_governance.quality_preservation: Criterion is output, not the clock (AS-103-08).

practitioner_frameworks.framework: COD deficit as a diagnostic lens

data_layer_constraints: A speed_task cannot be published without primary_quality and intended_adaptation. (AS-103-01)
A speed_task with information_demand: none cannot be tagged agility. (D103-6, AS-103-07)
A test_record cannot be published without construct_measured and recorded conditions. (AS-103-09, AS-103-10)
A test_record whose construct_measured conflicts with its test type is rejected at save. (AS-103-10)
No entity may expose a computed athlete score, composite speed index, automated training-priority recommendation, or automated progression instruction.
No field may store a G3-published universal sled load, rest ratio, velocity-decrement threshold, phase-boundary distance, angle progression, or change threshold as a course constant.
Free text containing an injury-prevention guarantee pattern is flagged for review before publication. (D103-12)
